status_summary: The White House released the National Security Strategy of the United States of America, dated November 2025, on 2025-12-04; it treats China within its Asia section, centered on rebalancing the economic relationship, deterrence and supply-chain resilience. It is a government-wide strategy rather than a standalone State and NSC paper offering a deep philosophical assessment of PRC designs, and no separate China-specific strategy document was found.

timeline.event: The White House released the National Security Strategy of the United States of America (dated November 2025), a general strategy with a section on China and the Indo-Pacific.

title: Draft a presidentially mandated 'Article X' strategy paper on the China challenge
uncertainties: The release date of 2025-12-04 rests on a law firm alert; the PDF itself is dated November 2025. The strategy text was read through a fetch summary, which found no standalone China strategy and no use of the phrase cost imposition. One search of general news for an Article X style China document found only think-tank material from earlier years, so a non-public or classified China strategy cannot be ruled out. A congressional reporting requirement for a China strategy was not searched. Judgment: a general strategy with a China section is treated as a parallel step at the low end of proposed; not_started would also be defensible.
